==Problem==
For any positive integer <imath>M</imath>, the notation <imath>M!</imath> denotes the product of the integers <imath>1</imath> through
<imath>M</imath>. What is the largest integer <imath>n</imath> for which <imath>5^n</imath> is a factor of the sum <imath>98!+99!+100!</imath> ?

<imath>\textbf{(A) }23 \qquad \textbf{(B) }24 \qquad \textbf{(C) }25 \qquad \textbf{(D) }26 \qquad \textbf{(E) }27</imath>

==Solution==
Factoring out <imath>98!+99!+100!</imath>, we have <imath>98! (1+99+99\cdot100)</imath>, which is <imath>98! (10000)</imath>. Next, <imath>98!</imath> has <imath>\left\lfloor\frac{98}{5}\right\rfloor + \left\lfloor\frac{98}{25}\right\rfloor = 19 + 3 = 22</imath> factors of <imath>5</imath>. The <imath>19</imath> is because of all the multiples of <imath>5</imath>.The <imath>3</imath> is because of all the multiples of <imath>25</imath>. Now, <imath>10,000</imath> has <imath>4</imath> factors of <imath>5</imath>, so there are a total of <imath>22 + 4 = \boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 26}</imath> factors of <imath>5</imath>.

~CHECKMATE2021

Note: Do you know what formula this uses? Most AMC 8 test takers won't know it. 
It's [[Legendre's Formula]].
